titulo: The maturity ladder: what is and isn't cultivated AI
lead: Not every AI with memory is cultivated, and not every agent is cultivated. Most of what is called AI today operates on the first two steps. The difference between the steps is not the model: it's what exists around it.
objetivo: classify any AI on the four-level ladder and say what it needs to become cultivation.

aprende.t: The four steps: executor, contextual, agent, and cultivated
What looks like cultivation and isn't

hero_alt: A stone staircase in a garden with four terraces, from bare soil to a full garden.

secoes.sub: Click each step to see the flow and an example.

nos.detalhe: No memory, no evaluation, no persistent context. Every interaction starts from zero. E.g., an FAQ chatbot that returns the most likely answer and never improves.
It remembers who you are and personalizes. But if it makes the same mistake ten times, nobody fixes the environment. E.g., an assistant that knows your name, job title, and calendar.
It reasons, picks tools, and acts. Without evaluation, it repeats mistakes indefinitely: it's sophisticated automation. E.g., it schedules meetings and books the wrong time five times in a row.

nos.sub: action → evaluation → feedback → adjustment → new run
nos.detalhe: Everything the agent does, plus the full cycle: every run is evaluated, mistakes become rules, and autonomy grows as consistency grows. The weights don't change; the garden does.

secoes.legenda: 1→2 adds memory and context. 2→3 adds tools and autonomy. 3→4 adds evaluation, feedback, and adjustment of the environment.
secoes.dica: Most implementations stop at step 2 or 3 and call it "advanced AI." Cultivation begins when the cycle closes.

texto: Memory is personalization and persistent context: "I know you prefer morning meetings." The next conversation starts from a richer base.
But the way the system decides, acts, and fails stays the same.
Cultivation is a change in behavior backed by evidence: it runs, fails, logs, analyzes, changes the rule, runs again, and compares.

exemplo.texto: Last week: 14/20 correct. This week: 18/20. Version 1.0 had 5 rules; 1.3 has 12, all coming from real mistakes.

texto: The system remembers you don't like long meetings and starts suggesting 30 minutes. If three 30-minute meetings fail because the topic didn't fit, it will keep suggesting 30.
Cultivation would say: "if the agenda has more than 3 items, suggest 45 minutes."
Memory answers: "what do you know about me?"
Cultivation answers: "what do you do differently today compared to last month, and why?" If the system can only answer the first, it has memory.

secoes.titulo: What looks like cultivation and isn't
secoes.sub: It works, it solves the problem, but it doesn't evolve.

texto: Wrong answer, you rephrase and try again. You learned to ask better; the system stays the same.
Looking up documents before answering improves accuracy, but if the wrong document was retrieved, nobody logs it. The system doesn't correct itself.
Fixed steps that always run the same way. If the email format changes, it breaks. An LLM node in the middle doesn't turn automation into an agent.
Reasons, uses tools, delivers. Nobody measures whether the result is good. It repeats the same mistakes with the same confidence.

secoes.sub: Copy it and fill it in for each AI you use.

blocos.conteudo:
# Which step my AI is on

## <tool or agent name>
Step (1 executor / 2 contextual / 3 agent / 4 cultivated): 
Does it have memory between sessions? yes / no
Does it have tools (does it act, not just answer)? yes / no
Does anyone measure whether the result was good? yes / no
Does the evaluation turn into a change in the environment? yes / no
Does the environment have versions (do I know what changed and when)? yes / no

Test: if it makes the same mistake tomorrow as today, what stops it?

What's missing for the next step:

secoes.titulo: The tool isn't cultivated; the architecture is

texto: OpenAI Codex + Agents API + Evals, Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, and LangGraph bring agent, memory, tools, and evaluation.
Claude Code and the Agent SDK have agent, memory, and tools; you build the evaluation with scripts, tests, and observability. The cycle closes, it just takes more work.
ChatGPT has memory and tools, but structured evaluation and feedback that changes the environment depend only on you.
A plain LLM through an API, and n8n/Make with a fixed flow. The same n8n moves up a category when it gains agents, persistent memory, and evaluation: the tool is the same, the architecture changed.

exercicios.texto: Use the classification sheet for three AIs you use (at work or in your personal life).
exercicios.pronto: all three sheets have a step marked and the "what's missing for the next step" line filled in.

exercicios.texto: Ask your main AI the two test questions: what it knows about you, and what it does differently today compared to last month.
exercicios.pronto: you noted whether it answered the second one with evidence (a concrete example of change) or not.

perguntas.p: An assistant remembers your name, job title, and calendar preferences, but books meetings at the wrong time every week. Which step is it on?
perguntas.explica: It personalizes (it has memory), but there's no cycle that corrects the mistake. Memory without evaluation is step 2.

perguntas.p: An n8n flow receives an email, calls an LLM to extract data, and saves it to a spreadsheet. Is it a cultivated agent?
opcoes: Yes, because it has an LLM
No: it's a fixed flow, with no reasoning, evaluation, or adjustment
Yes, if the model is state of the art
perguntas.explica: An LLM node in the middle doesn't change the architecture. Without evaluation and feedback, there's no cultivation.

perguntas.p: Which question separates memory from cultivation?
opcoes: What do you know about me?
What do you do differently today compared to last month, and why?
perguntas.explica: Memory answers the first one. Only a cultivated system answers the second with evidence.

perguntas.p: What do you need to add to move up from step 3 (agent) to step 4 (cultivated)?
opcoes: Evaluation, feedback, and adjusting the environment, with a new run
perguntas.explica: From 3 to 4, what comes in is the cycle: measure, correct the environment, and run again to compare. The model and tools were already there.

itens.texto: Memory makes the system know more; cultivation makes it make fewer mistakes.
If you make the same mistake tomorrow as today, what in the system stops it? If the answer is nothing, it isn't cultivation.
